title: XR text entry speed
bottleneck: Typing in XR is far slower than a physical keyboard: virtual keyboards lack tactile feedback, voice dictation needs correction, and novel methods (chorded, gaze-typing) have steep learning curves. Productivity tasks stall when text entry runs at a fraction of keyboard speed. No XR text method approaches 60+ wpm comfortably.
why_it_blocks: Text is the backbone of knowledge work; slow entry keeps XR out of offices. Until typing in XR is fast and effortless, headsets can't replace laptops.
current_state: Floating keyboards, swipe typing, and wrist-EMG typing research show progress, but comfortable high-speed XR text entry remains unsolved. Without tactile feedback every keypress needs visual confirmation, slowing entry further and increasing error rates. Chorded and gaze-based methods demand weeks of practice, a learning curve most users will not climb for a secondary device.
